_comment: Permissions policy for liftoff-github-deploy.
Scoped to what a deploy actually does under ECS Express Mode: push an image,
register a new task definition revision, and point the Express service at it.
It CANNOT create or delete services, clusters, or load balancers -- CI has no
business doing that, and a compromised workflow should not be able to tear down
or re-point your infrastructure.
UpdateExpressGatewayService is Resource:* because Express service ARNs are
generated at creation time and are not known when this policy is written. Tighten
it to the real ARN once the service exists -- see infra/README.md.
iam:PassRole now covers three roles, not two: Express Mode also needs the
infrastructure role passed, and to ecs.amazonaws.com rather than
ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com. Forgetting that is an AccessDenied on update with a
message that does not name the missing role.
ecr:GetAuthorizationToken must be Resource:* -- it is account-level with no
resource to scope to. Every other ECR action is pinned to the one repository.
Running the one-off migration task before the service rolls. Without
these the deploy ships code to a database that may not have its tables
-- which is exactly what happened when the maxes work auto-deployed.
RunTask is scoped to the liftoff-migrate family only, so this cannot be
used to run arbitrary task definitions. DescribeTasks and the log read
are how the workflow decides pass or fail: a migrate task that fails
must stop the deploy rather than let it roll over a broken schema.
Reading the migrate task's own output. Scoped to the one log group the
task writes to; the workflow prints it whether the task passed or
failed, because a failure with no log is unactionable.
